body: The proposed account identifies ambiguity as the primary friction point but recommends a solution that may reintroduce negotiation burdens. Characterizing the tracking system as static conflicts with the acknowledged reality of dynamic schedules; a static board requires dynamic maintenance, which necessitates the very conversations the group seeks to streamline. Additionally, the strategy to re-engage the avoiding friend assumes avoidance stems from conflict stress rather than overwhelm or shame. Inviting them to design a system may be perceived as additional labor, potentially deepening avoidance. Finally, the account does not specify who maintains the system, risking a shift of burden onto the non-avoiding friends.
